title: Missing return
prompt:
Why does this fail to compile?
`public int f(int x) { if (x > 0) return 1; }`
options: When `x <= 0`, execution reaches the end without returning an int
The method name is too short
explanation: The compiler proves every path returns. Add a final `return 0;` (or an else) to cover the x <= 0 path.

title: Predict the output: parameters are copies
prompt: `demo()` is called. Predict what each `println` prints.
explanation: `bump` receives a copy of `n`'s value; changing its own `x` never touches the caller's `n`, which stays 5. To get a new value out of a method, `return` it and assign it: `n = bumped(n)` makes n 6.

title: Wire up a helper
prompt: Complete the helper method declaration and the call.
explanation: Helpers are called by bare name inside the same class. The return type comes right before the method name.

title: Is it prime?
prompt: Return whether `n` is prime (n ≥ 2 counts only if divisible by nothing but 1 and itself; n < 2 is never prime). Loop trial divisors from 2 while `i * i <= n` — checking up to √n is the standard trick.

solution.explanation: Early-return on the first divisor found; if the loop survives, n is prime. Any factor above √n pairs with one below it, so `i * i <= n` is enough — O(√n) without computing a square root.

hints: This is the validation shape: look for a counterexample (a divisor) and bail out the moment you find one.
Handle `n < 2` first, then try divisors starting at 2 while `i * i <= n`.
`if (n % i == 0) return false;` inside the loop, `return true;` after it.

title: Drill: count with a helper
prompt: From memory: return how many of the three ints are even. Write a private helper `isEven(int x)` returning boolean, and call it three times. (Yes, you could inline it — the drill is writing a helper fluently.)

solution.explanation: The helper names one idea (`isEven`) so the main method reads like the problem statement. `x % 2 == 0` is also correct for negatives, since -2 % 2 is 0 and -3 % 2 is -1.

hints: Write the small yes/no question as its own method first, then use it from the main method.
Helper signature: `private boolean isEven(int x)` — it goes inside the same class braces, below `countEven`.
In `countEven`: `if (isEven(a)) count++;` and the same for `b` and `c`.
